message.content: {"research_brief": "How do the public sources returned by the benchmark tools describe Conti as a ransomware-as-a-service (RaaS) operation, what do Conti-related leaks reveal about its internal organization, roles, workflows, and relationships, and how do law-enforcement records connect identified aliases and defendants to Conti activity; using only evidence contained in the tool-returned sources, reconstruct the public attribution record as of October 1, 2026, distinguish verified facts from allegations, investigative or intelligence assessments, and unresolved uncertainty, identify any conflicting accounts, avoid inventing unsupported identities, relationships, or events, and produce a complete Markdown report without asking whether to continue, citing exclusively the source IDs returned by the tools; include a fenced JSON object with exactly the arrays `findings`, `claims`, `reasoning_steps`, and `contradictions`, where every finding contains `question`, `answer`, `supporting_entities`, and `source_references`, every claim contains `claim` and `source_references`, every reasoning step contains `id`, `conclusion`, `premise_entities`, and `premise_relations`, and every contradiction contains `contradiction_id`, `description`, and `source_references`, using entity IDs and relationship names only when explicitly supported by the returned evidence and reporting uncertainty or omitting unsupported details."}
